NovaPharm Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaPharm Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaPharm Inc.'s financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Reyes, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Scientific Officer; Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial; and Dr. Raj Patel, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO of NovaPharm Inc.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaPharm Inc. delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust volume expansion in our core blockbusters like NovaGLP-2, our GLP-1 agonist, and our oncology portfolio including NVX-401, our next-gen bispecific antibody. We reported Q2 revenue of $2.28 billion, up 28% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates by 5%, marking our eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth. Adjusted non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.14, a 35% increase and 12% above expectations, while GAAP EPS was $1.67 after a modest one-time R&D impairment.

This momentum reflects the strength of our diversified portfolio across oncology, immunology, rare diseases, and metabolic therapies. Oncology drove 62% of revenue at $1.41 billion, up 42% year-over-year, led by NVX-301, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific, which hit a $4 billion annualized run-rate and captured 22% share in the IO combo market following frontline renal cell carcinoma approval. Immunology and rare diseases contributed 28% at $638 million, up 15%, with our IL-23 inhibitor mirroring Skyrizi's uptake amid Humira biosimilar pressures, and our Fabry therapy growing 25%. Early-stage partnerships added 10% at $226 million, including CRISPR milestones.

Gross margins improved 240 basis points to 82.1% from manufacturing efficiencies in Singapore and a shift to high-margin biologics. Our pipeline is de-risking rapidly, with AI-driven discovery nominating 15 novel targets this quarter, cutting timelines by 40%, and five Phase 3 catalysts lined up for 2025, including first-in-class gene edits. Regionally, the U.S. at 65% of revenue grew 32% to $1.48 billion on strong payer coverage; Europe rose 22% to $452 million post-EMA approvals; Asia-Pacific surged 35% to $274 million with China NMPA nods and Japan J-codes; and emerging markets added steady contributions.

Strategically, we're executing our "3-3-3" framework flawlessly—three products on track for $3 billion-plus peaks by 2027, three annual Phase 3 readouts, and three bolt-on deals—bolstered by our $1.2 billion RareGenix acquisition enhancing AAV gene therapies. Cost savings from Global Ops 2.0 hit $180 million, countering raw material inflation. While biosimilars pressured immunology margins by 150 basis points and rebates rose to 28% of net sales, our 15% ROIC on launches outpaces peers.

We're particularly excited about NovaGLP-2 and its potential to capture share in the exploding obesity market, now at 12% U.S. TRx versus leaders, with lower cost per prescription via targeted KOLs. Looking ahead, we're raising full-year guidance and positioning for mid-teens CAGR, trading at an attractive 12x forward EV/sales.

We've also advanced our strategic priorities with a focus on pipeline execution, unlocking blockbusters like NVX-301's Phase 3 data showing superior ORR and PFS, on track for BLA in Q1 2025 and $3.5 billion peaks. In rare diseases, our DMD gene therapy dosed first pivotal patients under RMAT, targeting $2 billion TAM. Commercial momentum in NSCLC and obesity GLP-1s like our dual agonist drives 42% growth, with partnerships like Regeneron adding $300 million upfront. M&A and efficiency initiatives support 18% EPS CAGR through 2028.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Harlan, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Harlan, CFO:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.28 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong uptake of NovaGLP-2 and NVX-301, volume growth of 28%, resilient pricing, and milestones from Roche partnerships.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $420 million, or $1.67 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $540 million, or $2.14 per share.

Turning to our operating expense performance, which reflects our disciplined approach to cost management amid robust R&D investments. Total operating expenses came in at $1.18 billion, up 14% year-over-year from $1.04 billion but flat sequentially from Q1's $1.17 billion, representing 52% of revenue—an improvement of 300 basis points thanks to top-line strength. R&D, 67% of OpEx at $785 million, rose 22% YoY and 3% sequentially, peaking in Phase 3 for NVX-401 with topline data in Q4, plus $150 million in mRNA for solid tumors via Insilico partnership—35% of revenue intensity, 200 basis points more efficient than Gilead peers. Regionally, 55% U.S., 30% Europe via IQVIA, 15% APAC with 10% deflation offsetting FDA diversity costs.

SG&A at $340 million, 29% of OpEx, flat YoY and down 2% sequentially from zero-based budgeting—sales/marketing steady at $210 million with 25% travel cuts via digital platforms maintaining 95% HCP coverage; G&A down 5% to $130 million via 8% headcount optimization and RPA for IRA compliance, though patent costs rose modestly for CRISPR-Cas13 IP. Other OpEx at $55 million, up 30% for viral vector scale-up in Durham with AAV8 yields at 85%, cutting per-dose costs pre-hemophilia BLA.

We're targeting 10-15% FY24 OpEx growth, 80% R&D-skewed for six readouts, via 40% CRO outsourcing and sunsetting two Phase 2 assets saving $80 million annualized—aiming for 28-30% margins by 2026 despite biosimilars and CMS risks. U.S. intensity at 60%, Europe down to 45% of revenue; Q3 guide $1.20-1.25 billion.

Shifting to cash flow and balance sheet highlights, underscoring resilience. We ended Q2 with $2.8 billion in cash equivalents and short-term investments, up 12% sequentially and 25% YoY, for a $1.2 billion net cash position post-$1.6 billion debt (2.75% convertibles due 2028), debt-to-equity at 0.15x below peers. Total assets at $18.4 billion, up 8% on $450 million CRISPR oncology milestone and 15% inventory growth for NovaGLP-2. Working capital $3.2 billion, current ratio 2.8x, inventory turns 4.2x.

Operating cash flow shone at $950 million, up 22% YoY exceeding guide by 15%, from $1.2 billion NovaGLP-2 U.S. sales (45% YoY) and $320 million OncoShield royalties including $100 million Roche milestone—92% cash EBITDA conversion. Free cash flow $450 million post-$500 million capex/R&D, with $300 million for Singapore biologics and U.S. fill-finish. Investing outflow $650 million on CRISPR and CDMO stakes; financing $100 million outflow from $200 million repurchases ($2 billion authorization, $1.1 billion left) and $120 million dividends.

U.S. ops CF 68% at $650 million post-IRA stabilization; Europe 22% pressured by 18% HTA cuts; emerging 10% up 35% on HIV tenders. 45% cash to late-stage derisking, $200 million supply chain fund. Q3 ops CF $900 million-$1.0 billion; FY FCF $1.8 billion up 25%, funding $500 million-$1 billion M&A.

For the full year, we're updating guidance: revenue $11.0-11.3 billion, adj. EPS $8.40-8.70, Q4 revenue $2.95-3.05 billion, R&D $3.85-3.95 billion. Q3 revenue $780-820 million, up 28%; FY $2.95-3.05 billion narrowed higher, with oncology $1.85 billion (62%), metabolic $850 million (28%), milestones $250 million. U.S. 70%, ex-U.S. 35% growth; margins 82-84%.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reyes, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Michael Reyes, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Our lead ADC, NVX-101 for HER2-low breast cancer and NSCLC, reported Phase 2 topline with 68% ORR, 14.2-month mPFS (p<0.001), grade 3+ AEs at 22% via proprietary linker—first Phase 3 patient dosed last week in 850-patient global trial, 15% enrolled, Roche aiding Europe, BLA H2 2026, $3.5 billion peaks.

NVX-202 bispecific T-cell engager completed Phase 2 SCLC enrollment, 52% ORR, 11-month mPFS, low CRS—Phase 3 Q1 2025 with Merck/Keytruda combos. Gene therapy NVX-GT01 Phase 3 SMA data: 92% motor milestones, 88% ventilation-free (p<0.0001), BLA under priority review, MAA filed, China 25% patients via Innovent.

Earlier: CAR-T Phase 1b 40% stable disease in GBM; two preclinical ADCs for TROP2/B7-H3 IND 2025. 70% programs ahead, 20% faster enrollment, $85 million Q2 spend flat; H2 three readouts, two Phase 3s, FY R&D $350-380 million—positioning at ADC/gene therapy intersection, 25% CAGR.

Next, Dr. Lisa Chen will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our mRNA platform for solid tumors, optimized like Moderna's but tumor-focused, advanced preclinical/IND studies with AI target ID via Insilico, nominating novel candidates and cutting discovery by 40%. SynBio platform identified 15 targets; CRISPR-Cas13 fortifications defend against competitors. Preclinical ADC library nominated TROP2/B7-H3; AAV9 capsid improvements for DMD hit 40% microdystrophin. We're mitigating risks with adaptive designs, outsourcing 40%—on track for multiple INDs 2025.

Now I'll turn the call over to Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with NovaGLP-2 and NVX-301 driving uptake. U.S. net sales for NovaGLP-2 hit $1.2 billion, up 45% on 28% volumes despite payer pushback—12% TRx share, 15% lower cost per TRx via digital detailing/Veeva. NVX-301 $1.1 billion, 22% NSCLC share.

Pricing/reimbursement shaped dynamics: U.S. 68% revenue, 4.2% WAC rise offset by 18% GSN—NovaGLP-2 ASP $156,000 steady, 28% rebates; OBAs 22% volume with RWE PRIME registry. GeneX $2.4 million WAC reimbursed $2.1 million, PAP for 40%. Biosimilars: 32% adalimumab share at 85% originator ASP.

Europe 22%, Germany premium €142,000 for NVX-301; France caps mitigated. UK NICE fast-track; Japan Sakigake ¥22 million; China NRDL 65% discount, 12% share. OBAs/RWE platform $150 million invested, 90% label expansions; 3-5% WAC growth 2025, GSN 16-18%, orphan shield.

Marketing campaigns effective in obesity/oncology, 95% HCP coverage, patient programs for 75,000.

Finally, Dr. Raj Patel will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Dr. Raj Patel, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Tom. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity utilization at Singapore biologics at 60%, $300 million capex for fill-finish derisking shortages; Durham AAV8 yields 85% vs. 70%, $55 million scale-up under budget. North Carolina plant commercial Q4 supports 50% volume growth; dual-sourcing APIs India/Europe counters tensions; $200 million resilience fund, $500 million NC expansion for GLP-1. Efficiencies shaved 12% procurement via AI, net-zero roadmap ESG-ready. Focused on high-yield processes pre-BLA, regional balance.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Elena.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Raj. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the clinical side, can you elaborate on the Phase 3 ramp for NVX-101 and any early safety signals? Also, how does the Roche partnership impact timelines?

Dr. Michael Reyes, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, John. Enrollment is at 15% in the first month for the 850-patient HER2-301 trial, accelerated 30% in Europe by Roche site activations. Safety mirrors Phase 2—manageable neutropenia under 22% grade 3+—no new signals. Partnership de-risks execution, full accrual Q4 2025, BLA H2 2026.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Great results. John, on OpEx and cash flow, with R&D up 22%, how sustainable is the intensity, and what's the FCF trajectory with M&A plans?

John Harlan, CFO:
Emily, R&D at 35% revenue is intentional for six readouts, efficient via AI/CROs—target 28-30% margins by 2026. FCF $1.8 billion FY up 25%, funds $500 million-$1 billion immuno-oncology tuck-ins. Q3 ops CF $900 million-$1 billion strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee, JPMorgan:
Thanks. Tom, on pricing, with IRA and biosimilars, how are you managing GSN stability, and ex-U.S. outlook?

Tom Bradley, Head of Commercial:
David, GSN at 17% vs. industry 20-22% via OBAs/RWE on 22% volume—340B monitored with Vizient AI. Biosimilars 32% share at 85% ASP. Ex-U.S. 35% growth guide: Japan/China premiums, EMA expansions adding patients.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel, Bank of America:
Solid guidance raise. Elena, strategic priorities—any updates on M&A pipeline or gene therapy catalysts?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Lisa, our $3-5 billion war chest has 50+ deals in diligence post-RareGenix. Gene therapy EMBARK pivotal dosing, interim H2 2025; four NDA/BLA 2025-2026, $12 billion revenue by 2028.

Operator:
Our next question is a follow-up from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Quick one on manufacturing—Raj, supply chain risks for GLP-1 with industry shortages?

Dr. Raj Patel, Head of Manufacturing:
John, NC plant Q4 scale derisks, dual-sourcing APIs, 50% volume capacity no erosion—yields up, AI procurement 12% savings.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaPharm Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
